title: Fix: reduce metric cardinality in provision-to-ready step tags (remove per-node labels) + dashboard backfill
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Reduce Prometheus/OpenTelemetry series cardinality for provision-to-ready step metrics by removing per-node labels.
Update internal Grafana dashboards to query the new label set; backfill panels/variables to avoid broken views during rollout.
body:
Context
During the us-east A100 staged rollout we hit a metric series explosion (root cause: step metrics were tagged with per-node identifiers like node_id / instance_id / hostname). This made the provision-to-ready dashboards slow/unusable and created noisy alert behavior due to delayed scrapes. This PR is a follow-up hotfix to reduce cardinality while keeping the step breakdown usable for SLOs and rollouts.

What this changes
- Removes per-node labels from provision-to-ready step metrics emitted by the provisioning orchestrator + validation agent integration.
  - Removed labels: node_id, kube_node_name, cloud_instance_id, private_ip, validation_run_id
  - Kept labels (bounded): region, gpu_type, pool_id, image_channel, step, outcome (success|failure|timeout), failure_class (enum)
- Adds an explicit failure_class enum to replace “node_id + raw error message” as the primary slice for failure debugging.
- Moves node-level correlation to logs/traces:
  - node_id is still present in structured logs and in the per-node validation artifact record (readiness service), but is no longer exported as a metric label.
- Updates the dashboard JSON used by internal ops views:
  - Variables and panel queries updated to use failure_class and pool_id instead of node_id.
  - Adds a “Top failure classes (last 6h)” panel to preserve triage velocity.
- Adds guardrails/tests:
  - Unit test asserts that the exported label set matches the allowlist.
  - Lint check fails if new labels exceed the allowlist without updating the docs + review.

Why this is safe
- The time-to-ready SLI/SLO computations are based on event timestamps + readiness transitions (not node_id-tagged time series), so SLO math is unaffected.
- For node-specific triage we already rely on readiness artifacts + logs; this change formalizes that separation.

Implementation notes
- Metric names unchanged to avoid breaking downstream alert rules mid-rollout.
- Label rename strategy:
  - outcome is normalized ("success"|"failure"|"timeout")
  - step name is normalized to a fixed set (kebab-case) and validated in code.
- Example of the updated metric export:
  - Before: provision_to_ready_step_duration_seconds{step="nccl-smoke",node_id="node-9f3c...",kube_node_name="ip-10-...",region="us-east-1",gpu_type="a100"}
  - After:  provision_to_ready_step_duration_seconds{step="nccl-smoke",outcome="failure",failure_class="nccl_timeout",region="us-east-1",gpu_type="a100",pool_id="ded-us-east-a100-01",image_channel="candidate"}

Testing
- Unit tests: //controlplane/fleetreadiness/... (label allowlist test)
- Local: ran provisioning-metrics snapshot test against a sample validation run
- Staging: verified dashboard panels render under the staged rollout dataset (no node_id variables)

Rollout plan
- Ship behind existing staged rollout flag; this PR reduces risk immediately for us-east A100.
- After merge, SRE will re-enable the time-to-ready alerts that were temporarily downgraded to ticket-only during the incident.

Checklist
- [x] No per-node labels in exported metrics
- [x] Dashboard panels updated + verified
- [x] Label allowlist test added
- [x] SRE reviewed alert impact

Refs
- Incident thread: metric tag explosion during early rollout (internal)
- Related: ENG-4827 (step breakdown dashboards), ENG-4830 (flake/timeout follow-ups), SUP-28433 (nodes stuck in Validating; impacted by dashboard usability)
commits: controlplane/fleetreadiness: enforce metric label allowlist for provision-to-ready step metrics
provisioning/metrics: remove node-scoped labels; normalize outcome + step names; add failure_class enum
dashboards: update provisioning step breakdown panels/variables; add top failure_class panel
tests: add regression test ensuring node identifiers are not exported as metric labels
ci_checks: Build (pass); Unit tests (pass); Lint (pass); Dashboard JSON validation (pass).
review_conversation:
Allison Grant (requested changes): We can’t ship another unbounded label set. Please add an explicit allowlist + a unit test that fails if someone reintroduces node identifiers. Also normalize step names (we had both `nccl_smoke` and `nccl-smoke` in the same panel).

Sergio Costa (author): Added label allowlist + test; step names now validated against a fixed enum and normalized to kebab-case. Also removed validation_run_id label (was another hidden multiplier).

Aisha Bello: Do we lose any ability to find “which node is failing”? I’m OK losing that in metrics, but we need a clear alternative in the runbook / dashboards.

Sergio Costa (author): Agree. Added a dashboard link-out note: use readiness artifacts (node detail view) for node_id, and added a ‘Top failure classes’ panel so we can triage without node_id. Will follow up on runbook wording in ENG-4828 if needed.

Gabe Wilson: +1 on removing kube_node_name. One more ask: keep pool_id only if it’s bounded; do we have any dynamic pool_id generation that could explode?

Sergio Costa (author): pool_id is generated from the dedicated pool name (bounded by fleet config) and is already used elsewhere in dashboards. Added a comment in code explaining the assumption and where to review if that changes.

Benji Okafor: Can we ensure readiness service events aren’t also exporting node_id via exemplars in a way that breaks cardinality? (Different path, but same symptom.)

Sergio Costa (author): This PR doesn’t change exemplars; we’re not emitting exemplars to Prometheus right now. Added a TODO in docs to revisit exemplars once we have a retention plan.
